WCF Digital

Bring the billing work back into the system.

Restructuring hospital billing so officers could enter medical costs, review prices, and work within the required rules.

Explore the decisions ↓

Context

WCF Digital supports workmen’s compensation case management for Thailand’s Social Security Office. This case focuses on hospital billing: the point where treatment records, invoices, declared prices, and supporting documents meet.

My contribution

UX/UI design, workflow mapping & UAT support

I gathered requirements with experienced officers, mapped workflows and exceptions, designed WCF screens, and supported implementation, testing, and training with BA, SA, and developers. The team delivered the system; my responsibility was the design, not deployment or pricing policy.

Year
2025–2026
Project status
Live · 27 July 2026

01 / The problem

A billing screen existed. The complete task still happened elsewhere.

Legacy constraints prevented officers from entering all the required costs in the system. They prepared documents and calculations outside WCF, including Excel, then entered the results again. I needed to understand the work behind the form before reorganizing the interface.

02 / Design decisions

Start with the officer’s task, then organize the information.

I organized the billing work around the hospital and treatment period, with invoices, treatment categories, medical items, and supporting documents kept in context.

  1. 01Compensation case→
  2. 02Hospital / treatment period→
  3. 03Invoice or receipt→
  4. 04Treatment category & medical items
  1. 01

    Separate the categories

    Medical supplies are divided into types 1, 2, and 3, so officers can enter each item within the appropriate group.

  2. 02

    Enter several items together

    Officers can select multiple medical items, set quantities, review their selection, and save the batch.

  3. 03

    Keep the price comparison visible

    Charged, eligible, and declared amounts appear together for review. A mismatch prompts a warning and correction of the source document, rather than silently changing the amount.

03 / What happened

A flow users could complete under the required rules.

During training and UAT, I observed users understanding the revised flow and completing the required entry tasks. The delivered design supported billing work from entry and category review through document output in the tested flow.

● Live · 27 July 2026

The system went live on 27 July 2026. The observations above come from training and UAT; I do not have production measurements for time saved or error reduction.

04 / What I learned

Usability also means respecting what the system cannot decide.

The most important design work was making the rules and exceptions understandable at the point of entry. A cleaner screen was useful only if officers could complete the real task and know when a document needed correction.

Design screens and the legacy interface are shown as project evidence. Launch status and qualitative observations are based on my project experience.
